I. GENERAL
Women and children have become a serious concern of the international community, considering their vulnerable position as victims of violence and discrimination from their families and environment. Various acts of violence against both women and children within the household as well as outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the Government of Magelang Regency is obligated to provide protection to women and children against acts of violence and discrimination which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 35 of 2014 Concerning Amendments to Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection for women and children against acts of violence and discrimination is an obligation of the Regional Government in the context of regional autonomy, which is manifested in the form of Regional Regulations as stipulated in Article 236 paragraph (1), Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government.

On that basis, the Regional Government of Magelang Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children, including by issuing Regent Regulation Number 26 of 2010 Concerning The existence of these regulations is felt to be not yet capable of providing maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence and discrimination that occur in the social life of society. In addition to the problem of these laws and regulations, the factor of low public understanding of the rights of women and children has implications for the low legal awareness -17- of the community to report acts of violence or utilize the facilities provided by the Law to resolve their problems.

Based on these considerations, a regulation is needed in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children against acts of violence and discrimination that is able to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children against acts of violence and discrimination that occur.

This Regional Regulation is intended to provide responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. This regional regulation also regulates the rights of victims of violence, Handling of Victims of violence, Government Responsibility up to the Participation of Government, Society and Family in the prevention and resolution of violence and discrimination against women and children.

In its implementation, the Regional Government is also allowed to establish cooperation with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding arrangements sourced from the State Budget, Regional Budget, Village Budget as well as from the government, Regional Government or other Sources that are not binding are expected to guarantee the implementation of protection for women and children against victims of violence and discrimination.

CHAPTER V
SERVICES FOR VICTIMS OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE AND DISCRIMINATION Article 7 (1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide services to women and children victims of acts of violence and discrimination.
(2) Services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to witnesses and/or victims of violence and discrimination.
(3) In the context of services as referred to in paragraph (1), a Standard Operating Procedure for Services shall be prepared.

Article 2
Letter a The principle of respect for human rights serves as the foundation for the concept of protection of women and children victims of violence and discrimination, constituting respect for human rights and the dignity and worth of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).
Letter b The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women -18- to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
Letter c The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children victims of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.
Letter d The principle of victim protection, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities and Regional Governments to fulfill the rights of women and victims of acts of violence as regulated in laws and regulations.
Letter e The principle of Empowerment is that every effort to protect women and children victims of violence must be oriented towards efforts to strengthen victims physically, psychologically, socially and economically.
Letter f The principle of integration means that the series of activities to provide protection to women and children victims of violence will be implemented jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation.

Article 22
The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence and discrimination organized by the Regional Government through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Regent and/or to the DPRD.

Pasal 1 angka 8 defines “Kekerasan terhadap perempuan” as actions causing suffering “secara fisik, seksual atau psikologis,” and Pasal 1 angka 9 defines “Kekerasan terhadap anak” including suffering “seksual.” These provisions were present in the retrieved English candidates ([1.2-0] / [2.2-2] style definition block appears in the retrieved set as [1.2-0] header and similar definitions exist in the corpus; however for 1.2 the retrieved set did not include the definition block, but the policy’s scope clearly covers sexual violence as a category). Given the policy’s explicit inclusion of ‘seksual,’ the correct label is Yes; the judge’s rationale that sexual violence is not explicitly mentioned is incorrect.

CHAPTER VII
INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK
Article 14
(1) In the context of providing services to women and children victims of violence and discrimination as referred to in Article 7, the Regional Government shall establish an Institution with the name Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and -11- Children (P2TP2A) or similar institutions that have the same functions and roles as a service center in the protection of women and children from acts of violence and discrimination.

Letter f The principle of integration means that the series of activities to provide protection to women and children victims of violence will be implemented jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation.

Article 18
Paragraph (1) Cooperation is carried out in the form of, among others, exchange and information, rehabilitation of victims of violence, repatriation and social reintegration as well as cooperation in the field of prevention, handling and recovery of women and children victims of violence and discrimination Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.

5.2.rationale: In the Indonesian source, there is no clear stakeholder-engagement mechanism specifically involving religious organizations/leaders. The only relevant mention is in the explanation of Pasal 6 huruf i: “hak atas pendampingan” may include “rohaniwan” (religious clergy) alongside psychologists, advocates, and family. That indicates possible types of companions/assistants for victims, not an engagement/collaboration policy with religious institutions for prevention or service delivery. The retrieved candidates reflect this same limited mention ([5.2-39]). Therefore the judge’s No is reasonable; the golden label Yes appears incorrect for this document.
